common_name: Elizabeth Passionflower (Purple-and-White Vigorous Hybrid Passion Vine)

planting.note: Plant container vines after last frost in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Elizabeth bears large, showy purple-and-white flowers on a vigorous hybrid passion vine.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun and provide a trellis or fence for the vigorous tendrils. Elizabeth bears large, intricately structured flowers combining deep purple filaments with white and lavender petals, a striking hybrid passionflower display on a fast-growing, heavily blooming vine. It draws pollinators readily during its long summer bloom season, and while it can produce fruit, it is grown chiefly for its exceptional flower display. In zones at the cooler edge of its range it dies back to the ground in winter and regrows strongly from deep roots in spring; mulch the crown heavily where marginal.

common_name: Amethyst Passionflower (Deep Purple Fringed Flower Vigorous Vine)

planting.note: Plant container vines after last frost in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Amethyst bears deep, saturated purple flowers with a fine, fringed filament corona on a vigorous, fast-growing vine.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun and provide a trellis or fence for the vigorous tendrils. Amethyst bears deep, rich purple flowers with a fine, densely fringed filament corona, an intensely colored bloom that has made it a popular hybrid for gardeners seeking a bolder purple than the paler blue-lavender of the straight species. It flowers heavily through summer and draws pollinators readily. In zones at the cooler edge of its range it dies back to the ground in winter and regrows strongly from deep roots in spring; mulch the crown heavily where marginal.

common_name: Constance Eliott Passionflower (Fragrant Pure White Hardy Passion Vine)

planting.note: Plant container vines after last frost in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Constance Eliott is a fragrant, pure white-flowered selection of the cold-hardy blue passionflower.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun and provide a trellis or fence for the vigorous tendrils; Constance Eliott shares the exceptional cold hardiness of its parent species, blue passionflower, tolerating brief dips to 10 to 15 degrees Fahrenheit when established roots are protected by mulch. It bears creamy pure-white flowers with a soft, sweet fragrance, a cleaner, more subtle color than the blue-and-purple typical of the species, followed by oval orange-yellow fruits that are edible but mild-flavored. Dies to the ground in zones 7-8 but regrows strongly from deep roots; do not remove dormant crowns too early in spring.
